front_matter.preface: Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga, compiled and translated by Rev. William Pettigrew (American Baptist Mission House, Ukhrul, Manipur, Assam, 1907, 2nd Edition; printed at Baptist Mission Press, Calcutta). Preserves the earliest published Christian hymnal and devotional poetry in the Ukhrul dialect of Tangkhul Naga.

table_of_contents.title: Hymns of the Kingdom & Eternal Life

chapters.title: Early Devotional Hymns
chapters.summary: Classic devotional hymns including 'Jesus Loves Me' (Hi Jesuna Laishi).
chapters.tangkhul_text: 1. Hi Jesuna laishi, khikala jila, in a Vare chiwui lairikli, palaga I shitsanga. Ma, ili laishi! Ma, ili laishi! Ma, ili laishi! Lairikli iya. 2. Hi Jesuna laishi, A mangla chihomihai; Varina kaching khamaug shomida changmilakra. 3. Ili Jesuna laishi, noshino awui nona; athum masathukmana, Ana kamakangvana. 4. Hi Jesuna laishi, iwui moral pheomira; khikala jila awui Mangla chihomihaira.
chapters.english_translation: 1. Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so; little ones to Him belong, they are weak but He is strong. Yes, Jesus loves me! The Bible tells me so. 2. Jesus loves me, He who died heaven's gate to open wide; He will wash away my sin. 3. Jesus loves me, loves me still, though I'm very weak and ill; from His shining throne on high. 4. Jesus loves me, He will stay close beside me all the way; He has washed away my sin.
grammar_points: Early orthography feature: 'ai' diphthong where TLS standardizes to 'ei'.
comprehension_questions: How is divine love expressed in early Pettigrew Tangkhul hymnody?
What orthographic differences distinguish the 1907 text from modern TLS spelling?

chapters.title: Hymns of Divine Grace & Love
chapters.summary: Grace and security in faith: 'Safe in the Arms of Jesus' (He Jesuwui Makali).
chapters.tangkhul_text: 1. He Jesuwui makali, eingphalaka; siwui ngahan ngaida romhai, phasa kakhanang rai. Kachingwui chan nganalu, iwui la sada laili, Jesuna nani mashitta, hangda la kasana. 2. He Jesuwui makali, kangachee malaimana; I moral maphungmara, chiaina makhanangmara. Wukli kakhanang malaita, ringkapha apamna, mikumo awui okkathui ringkapha kashungna.
chapters.english_translation: 1. Safe in the arms of Jesus, safe on His gentle breast; there by His love o'ershaded, sweetly my soul shall rest. Hark! 'tis the voice of angels, borne in a song to me. 2. Safe in the arms of Jesus, safe from corroding care; safe from the world's temptations, sin cannot harm me there. Free from the blight of sorrow, free from my doubts and fears.
grammar_points: Negative particle malaimana indicating complete absence.
comprehension_questions: What metaphor is used to express spiritual peace in Chapter 2?
Identify the negative verbal constructions in the stanzas.

chapters.title: Penitential & Supplication Hymns
chapters.summary: Supplication and fellowship: 'What a Friend We Have in Jesus' (Jesuli Ithum Kaphā Temi).
chapters.tangkhul_text: 1. Jesuli ithum kaphā temi akha leiyi, ithumwui moral kala kakhanang saikora phungmiya. Khorum-ngacheida Varili kachiphun mathaloikhalang, ningkhamayung tarakha ithum khamatai thotna. 2. Khipana kakhanang kala ningkachuk phunga? Jesuwui lili vashitlaga khorumlu. Ana khipakha matheikhui-mana malei, ningchang lak eina temkhamishi phapharomei.
chapters.english_translation: 1. What a friend we have in Jesus, all our sins and griefs to bear! What a privilege to carry everything to God in prayer! O what peace we often forfeit, O what needless pain we bear. 2. Have we trials and temptations? Is there trouble anywhere? We should never be discouraged; take it to the Lord in prayer. In His arms He'll take and shield thee; thou wilt find a solace there.
grammar_points: Dative case marker -li in personal relations ('Jesuli', 'Varili').
comprehension_questions: What is the Tangkhul equivalent for 'prayer' in Pettigrew's text?
Translate into Tangkhul: 'Jesus is our faithful friend.'

chapters.title: Pilgrim & Faith Hymns
chapters.summary: Unshakable refuge: 'Rock of Ages' (Aching Lungrei Makatha).
chapters.tangkhul_text: 1. Aching lungrei iwui vang kakhayei, nawui khamangli ili kaphumpam milu. Nawui azing eina kathur tara kala ashi china iwui moral shiman ngasaku. 2. Iwui pang eina kasa otna nawui shiyan makhararthukmana; kachara zangzang shoklala nawui akhavawuina. Na vathot iwui kachiphun, nawui crossli i panglakha ngaranmida leiyi.
chapters.english_translation: 1. Rock of Ages, cleft for me, let me hide myself in Thee; let the water and the blood, from Thy wounded side which flowed, be of sin the double cure, save from wrath and make me pure. 2. Not the labors of my hands can fulfill Thy law's demands; could my zeal no respite know, could my tears forever flow, all for sin could not atone; Thou must save, and Thou alone.
grammar_points: Causative suffix -sak in 'shiman ngasaku' (cause to disappear).
comprehension_questions: Explain the geological metaphor of 'Aching lungrei' in Tangkhul hymnody.
Identify the causative verbs in Chapter 4.

chapters.title: Hymns of the Kingdom & Eternal Life
chapters.summary: The heavenly river: 'Shall We Gather at the River' (Kongreili Ithum Ngazipra).
chapters.tangkhul_text: 1. Kaching Kazingramwui kongreili, Varewui khamatha apamli, ithum saikora ngazipra? Ma, ithum ngazipra kong kaphali, kong kaphali, Varewui kuiram ngachaili ngazipsera. 2. Kongrei chihui ngashilakna, thikahai maleimana; Vare eina A Naochina karing khangarum ramli.
chapters.english_translation: 1. Shall we gather at the river, where bright angel feet have trod, with its crystal tide forever flowing by the throne of God? Yes, we'll gather at the river, the beautiful river. 2. On the margin of the river, washing up its silver spray, we will walk and worship ever, all the happy golden day.
grammar_points: Repetition of nouns for poetic emphasis: 'kong kaphali, kong kaphali'.
comprehension_questions: What celestial imagery is depicted in the hymn?
How is collective gathering expressed morphologically?

chapters.title: Morning, Evening & Daily Life Hymns
chapters.summary: Evening meditation: 'Abide With Me' (I Eina Pamchinglu).
chapters.tangkhul_text: 1. Zimik tunhaira, ngaya kaching chuiye; Kazing khayingli i eina pamchinglu. Katei ngashunkhami kacham chitharanli, khangachamwui Ava, i eina pamchinglu. 2. Okkathui mirin hi thakta kanthuiseri; kuipham, ngashan saikora themthuira. Khamatei malei nawui ngachaili pamlu; Makangateipa, i eina pamchinglu.
chapters.english_translation: 1. Abide with me: fast falls the eventide; the darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide. When other helpers fail and comforts flee, Help of the helpless, O abide with me. 2. Swift to its close ebbs out life's little day; earth's joys grow dim; its glories pass away; change and decay in all around I see; O Thou who changest not, abide with me.
grammar_points: Continuous aspect suffix -ching in imperative pam-ching-lu.
comprehension_questions: What does the phrase 'zimik tunhaira' signify in Tangkhul life?

chapters.title: Doxologies, Anthems & Closing Liturgy
chapters.summary: Old Hundredth Doxology and The Lord's Prayer (Ithumwui Ava Kazingramli Kapam).
chapters.tangkhul_text: Vare khamatha kashungli, ngalei miyur saikorana matheilu; Kaching Kazingramwui mangla bing, Vare A Mingli mathaseru. Ava, A Nao, kala Mangla Kathara, ngashan kashung kumching-kumching leiyangranu. Amen. Ithumwui Ava Kazingramli kapam, Nawui ming kathara thada kharing sairanu. Nawui ngashan ram raranu. Nawui ning Kazingramli thada ngaleili la ngarunsangranu. Aja ithumwui kasala kashakpei milu. Ithumli kateina kashikhami pheomikahai thada ithumwui moralla pheomilu. Ithumli ngasateikhavaili mathalukhavai masangasaklu, kha kashieina kankhuimilu. Amen.
chapters.english_translation: Praise God from whom all blessings flow; praise Him all creatures here below; praise Him above, ye heavenly host; praise Father, Son, and Holy Ghost. Amen. Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever. Amen.
comprehension_questions: Quote the opening sentence of the Tangkhul Lord's Prayer.
Explain the optative inflection in Christian liturgical Tangkhul.

colophon.title: Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga

excerpts.tangkhul_text: 1. Hi Jesuna laishi, khikala jila, in a Vare chiwui lairikli, palaga I shitsanga. Ma, ili laishi! Ma, ili laishi! Ma, ili laishi! Lairikli iya. 2. Hi Jesuna laishi, A mangla chihomihai; Varina kaching khamaug shomida changmilakra. 3. Ili Jesuna laishi, noshino awui nona; athum masathukmana, Ana kamakangvana. 4. Hi Jesuna laishi, iwui moral pheomira; khikala jila awui Mangla chihomihaira.
excerpts.translation_en: 1. Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so; little ones to Him belong, they are weak but He is strong. Yes, Jesus loves me! The Bible tells me so. 2. Jesus loves me, He who died heaven's gate to open wide; He will wash away my sin. 3. Jesus loves me, loves me still, though I'm very weak and ill; from His shining throne on high. 4. Jesus loves me, He will stay close beside me all the way; He has washed away my sin.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Hymns of Divine Grace & Love
excerpts.tangkhul_text: 1. He Jesuwui makali, eingphalaka; siwui ngahan ngaida romhai, phasa kakhanang rai. Kachingwui chan nganalu, iwui la sada laili, Jesuna nani mashitta, hangda la kasana. 2. He Jesuwui makali, kangachee malaimana; I moral maphungmara, chiaina makhanangmara. Wukli kakhanang malaita, ringkapha apamna, mikumo awui okkathui ringkapha kashungna.
excerpts.translation_en: 1. Safe in the arms of Jesus, safe on His gentle breast; there by His love o'ershaded, sweetly my soul shall rest. Hark! 'tis the voice of angels, borne in a song to me. 2. Safe in the arms of Jesus, safe from corroding care; safe from the world's temptations, sin cannot harm me there. Free from the blight of sorrow, free from my doubts and fears.

excerpts.tangkhul_text: 1. Jesuli ithum kaphā temi akha leiyi, ithumwui moral kala kakhanang saikora phungmiya. Khorum-ngacheida Varili kachiphun mathaloikhalang, ningkhamayung tarakha ithum khamatai thotna. 2. Khipana kakhanang kala ningkachuk phunga? Jesuwui lili vashitlaga khorumlu. Ana khipakha matheikhui-mana malei, ningchang lak eina temkhamishi phapharomei.
excerpts.translation_en: 1. What a friend we have in Jesus, all our sins and griefs to bear! What a privilege to carry everything to God in prayer! O what peace we often forfeit, O what needless pain we bear. 2. Have we trials and temptations? Is there trouble anywhere? We should never be discouraged; take it to the Lord in prayer. In His arms He'll take and shield thee; thou wilt find a solace there.

excerpts.tangkhul_text: 1. Aching lungrei iwui vang kakhayei, nawui khamangli ili kaphumpam milu. Nawui azing eina kathur tara kala ashi china iwui moral shiman ngasaku. 2. Iwui pang eina kasa otna nawui shiyan makhararthukmana; kachara zangzang shoklala nawui akhavawuina. Na vathot iwui kachiphun, nawui crossli i panglakha ngaranmida leiyi.
excerpts.translation_en: 1. Rock of Ages, cleft for me, let me hide myself in Thee; let the water and the blood, from Thy wounded side which flowed, be of sin the double cure, save from wrath and make me pure. 2. Not the labors of my hands can fulfill Thy law's demands; could my zeal no respite know, could my tears forever flow, all for sin could not atone; Thou must save, and Thou alone.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Hymns of the Kingdom & Eternal Life
excerpts.tangkhul_text: 1. Kaching Kazingramwui kongreili, Varewui khamatha apamli, ithum saikora ngazipra? Ma, ithum ngazipra kong kaphali, kong kaphali, Varewui kuiram ngachaili ngazipsera. 2. Kongrei chihui ngashilakna, thikahai maleimana; Vare eina A Naochina karing khangarum ramli.
excerpts.translation_en: 1. Shall we gather at the river, where bright angel feet have trod, with its crystal tide forever flowing by the throne of God? Yes, we'll gather at the river, the beautiful river. 2. On the margin of the river, washing up its silver spray, we will walk and worship ever, all the happy golden day.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Morning, Evening & Daily Life Hymns
excerpts.tangkhul_text: 1. Zimik tunhaira, ngaya kaching chuiye; Kazing khayingli i eina pamchinglu. Katei ngashunkhami kacham chitharanli, khangachamwui Ava, i eina pamchinglu. 2. Okkathui mirin hi thakta kanthuiseri; kuipham, ngashan saikora themthuira. Khamatei malei nawui ngachaili pamlu; Makangateipa, i eina pamchinglu.
excerpts.translation_en: 1. Abide with me: fast falls the eventide; the darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide. When other helpers fail and comforts flee, Help of the helpless, O abide with me. 2. Swift to its close ebbs out life's little day; earth's joys grow dim; its glories pass away; change and decay in all around I see; O Thou who changest not, abide with me.
